title: Reported statements and tense shifts
objectives: Apply common backshifts in a specified context.
Distinguish say from tell in basic reporting patterns.

explanation.heading: Meaning and use
paragraphs: Reported speech describes what someone said without necessarily repeating their exact words. In direct speech, we might write: Maya said, ‘I am tired.’ In reported speech, a person could later say: ‘Maya said that she was tired.’ The pronoun changes because the reporter is talking about Maya rather than speaking as Maya.

When the reporting verb is in the past, a tense in the original statement often shifts back: am can become was, have finished can become had finished, and will can become would. This is called backshift. It is a common pattern, not a mechanical rule that applies in every situation.

explanation.heading: Form
paragraphs: Use say without a direct object when you name only the reported message: ‘Maya said that she was tired’. Use tell with a person as its object: ‘Maya told me that she was tired’. That is often optional after said or told: ‘She said she was tired’ is also possible.

Common backshifts include present simple to past simple, present continuous to past continuous, present perfect to past perfect, and will to would: ‘I work’ can become ‘she worked’; ‘I am working’ can become ‘she was working’; ‘I have finished’ can become ‘she had finished’; and ‘I will call’ can become ‘she would call’. Pronouns and possessive words change according to who is speaking and being reported.

explanation.heading: Examples in context
paragraphs: Time and place expressions sometimes change because the reporter's viewpoint is different. If a statement was made on Monday about Tuesday, a report written after Tuesday may use ‘the next day’ rather than ‘tomorrow’. Likewise, here may become there when the reporter is in another place. These changes depend on the actual situation, not just on the words in the original sentence.

Read the examples below. If Ana said ‘I am busy’ and you report her words later, ‘Ana said she was busy’ is a common backshift. If she is still busy and the fact remains relevant, ‘Ana said she is busy’ can also be possible. The choice affects how directly the report connects the statement to the present.

explanation.heading: Contrasts and common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not automatically backshift a fact merely because the reporting verb is past. A reporter can keep a present form when the fact is still true or presented as generally true: ‘The teacher said that water boils at 100°C at standard pressure’. A backshifted report may also be possible in many contexts. Choose a form that matches the intended viewpoint.

Do not write ‘She told that she was tired’ without an object in this pattern. Say ‘She told me that she was tired’ or ‘She said that she was tired’. A report represents what was said; it does not necessarily mean the reporter knows the statement is true. In controlled transformations, follow any specified viewpoint and backshift instruction.

examples.sentence: Maya said that she was tired.
examples.note: She refers to Maya; was is a common backshift from am.

examples.sentence: Maya told me that she was tired.
He said he worked from home.
examples.note: Worked can report a present simple statement with backshift.
Was working can report am working with backshift.
Had finished can report have finished with backshift.
Would can report will with backshift.

examples.sentence: The teacher said water boils at 100°C at standard pressure.
examples.note: The present form can remain for a generally true fact.

examples.sentence: On Monday she said she would leave the next day.
examples.note: The next day identifies Tuesday from the Monday viewpoint.

common_errors.incorrect: She told that she was tired.
common_errors.correct: She told me that she was tired.
common_errors.reason: Tell needs a person as its object in this pattern.

common_errors.incorrect: Maya said that she were tired.
common_errors.correct: Maya said that she was tired.
common_errors.reason: She takes was in the requested backshifted report.

common_errors.incorrect: She said me that she was busy.
common_errors.correct: She told me that she was busy.
common_errors.reason: Use told with the person me in this pattern.

summary: Reported speech presents a statement from the reporter’s viewpoint.
Past reporting verbs often allow backshift, but it is not always required.
Use say without a direct person object and tell with a person object in these patterns.

exercises.prompt: Maya said: “I am tired.” Report her statement with backshift.
exercises.explanation: She refers to Maya and was is the requested backshift.

options.text: Maya said I am tired.
Maya told she is tired.
Maya said she was tired.
Maya said she will tired.

option_feedback.a: “Maya said I am tired.” does not fit here. She refers to Maya and was is the requested backshift.
option_feedback.b: “Maya told she is tired.” does not fit here. She refers to Maya and was is the requested backshift.
option_feedback.c: “Maya said she was tired.” fits here. She refers to Maya and was is the requested backshift.
option_feedback.d: “Maya said she will tired.” does not fit here. She refers to Maya and was is the requested backshift.

option_feedback.d: “Ben told that he called.” does not fit here. Would call is the requested backshift of will call.
